items.prompt: A DeskPilot ticket is closed. Which statuses may it transition to?
items.answer: Only in_progress - closed tickets can be reopened, but not resolved, blocked or sent back to open
distractors: None - closed is terminal
open or in_progress
Any status except closed itself
items.explanation: rules.closed is ["in_progress"]. Note that nothing anywhere transitions back to open; open only appears as a starting status.

items.prompt: transitionTicket is asked to move a blocked ticket to blocked. What happens?
items.answer: The ticket is returned unchanged - no error, no write, and no status_changed event
distractors: TransitionError, because blocked is not in blocked's allowed list
The ticket is rewritten and a status_changed event from blocked to blocked is logged
The ticket's updatedAt is bumped but no event is logged
items.explanation: The same-status check returns early, before the rules lookup, so idempotent requests are harmless.

items.prompt: What happens to a ticket that has been merged into another one?
items.answer: It can no longer transition (TransitionError 'Merged tickets cannot transition.') and it is hidden from listTickets
distractors: It transitions together with the ticket it was merged into
It is deleted from the JSON store at merge time
It can still transition, but only to closed
items.explanation: transitionTicket rejects isMerged tickets, and listTickets filters out ticket.isMerged. The record stays in the store, pointing at mergedIntoId.

items.prompt: Two createTicket calls for the same org run concurrently. Both readDb before either writes. What can the stored file end up with?
items.answer: Only one of the two tickets - each writes its own full copy of the database, so the later write erases the earlier ticket (and both computed the same ticketNumber)
distractors: Both tickets, because writeQueue serializes the writes
Both tickets with the same ticketNumber, but nothing is lost
Neither ticket, because the second write detects the conflict and aborts
items.explanation: writeQueue only orders the writeFile calls; the read-modify-write cycle around them is not serialized. Each caller serializes the whole db object it read, so the second write replaces the first.

items.prompt: A successful transitionTicket call: how many readDb and writeDb calls does it make in total?
items.answer: 3 readDb and 2 writeDb - getTicketById, setTicketStatus and addTransitionEvent each read the whole database; the last two each write it back
distractors: 1 readDb and 1 writeDb, in a single transaction
2 readDb and 1 writeDb
3 readDb and 3 writeDb
items.explanation: Each store function opens its own read-modify-write cycle. The status change and its event are separate writes, so a failure between them leaves a status change with no audit event.

items.prompt: A resolved ticket is reopened (resolved -> in_progress). What happens to its resolvedAt?
items.answer: It keeps the old timestamp - resolvedAt is set on resolved/closed but never cleared on reopen
distractors: It is cleared to null
It is set to the reopen time
It is moved into a reopenedAt field
items.explanation: setTicketStatus only assigns resolvedAt when the new status is resolved or closed; there is no branch that resets it, so reports can show an in-progress ticket as resolved.

items.prompt: On a new ticket, an agent first adds an internal note, then a customer comments, then the agent replies publicly. Which comment sets firstResponseAt?
items.answer: The agent's public reply - internal notes and customer comments never count as a first response
distractors: The internal note, since it is the first agent comment
The customer's comment, since it is the first public comment
None - firstResponseAt is only set by a status transition
items.explanation: The condition is !ticket.firstResponseAt && authorType === "agent" && !isInternal; it is set once and never moved.

items.prompt: A comment body is  Tom & Jerry <b>  . What bodyHtml is stored?
items.answer:
Tom & Jerry <b>

- the body is trimmed and only < and > are escaped; & is left as-is
distractors:
Tom & Jerry <b>

- every HTML special character is escaped

Tom & Jerry

- the body is stored unescaped

Tom & Jerry

- only ampersands are escaped
items.explanation: bodyHtml is built with replaceAll("<", "<").replaceAll(">", ">") on the trimmed body. Ampersands and quotes pass through untouched.

items.prompt: updateTicketFields is called with exactly the ticket's current subject and priority. What changes?
items.answer: updatedAt is bumped and the file is rewritten, but no ticket.updated event is logged
distractors: Nothing at all - the function returns before writing
updatedAt is bumped and an empty ticket.updated event is logged
An error is thrown because no field changed
items.explanation: updatedAt = nowIso() runs unconditionally; the event push is guarded by Object.keys(newValue).length > 0. The ticket jumps to the top of the updatedAt-sorted list anyway.

items.prompt: updateTicketFields receives tags [" vip", "vip", "", "billing"]. What does the ticket store?
items.answer: ["vip", "billing"] - tags are trimmed, empty ones dropped, duplicates removed in first-seen order
distractors: [" vip", "vip", "billing"] - only empty tags are dropped
["billing", "vip"] - tags are deduplicated and sorted
[" vip", "vip", "", "billing"] - tags are stored as sent
items.explanation: Array.from(new Set(tags.map(trim).filter(Boolean))) - a Set keeps insertion order. The event is only logged if the JSON of the new list differs from the old one.

items.prompt: Org A has tickets numbered 1-7 and org B has 1-30. What ticketNumber does org A's next ticket get?
items.answer: 8 - numbering is the per-org maximum plus one
distractors: 31 - numbers are global across orgs
38 - the total ticket count plus one
A random UUID-derived number
items.explanation: nextTicketNumber filters to the org and reduces with Math.max starting at 0.

items.front: What does the writeQueue promise chain in store.ts guarantee, and what does it not?
items.back: It guarantees writeFile calls never overlap (no interleaved, corrupt JSON). It does not serialize read-modify-write cycles, so concurrent updates can still overwrite each other.

items.front: How does getTimeline build a ticket's timeline?
items.back: It maps comments and ticket events into one tagged union (kind: comment | event), concatenates them, and sorts by createdAt ascending with localeCompare on ISO strings.

items.front: What does parseNonEmptyString(value) return for a number, for "   ", and for "  hi  "?
items.back: null for a non-string; null for whitespace-only (trimmed length below min 1); "hi" trimmed for a valid string (max length 500 by default).
